clue.text: Platonic affair that left something lacking for Horatio?

definitions.text: Platonic affair that left something lacking for Horatio?

parts.words: Platonic affair that left something lacking for Horatio?
parts.note: Plato's line of thought, and Hamlet's remark to Horatio that heaven and earth hold more things than are dreamt of in his way of thinking

explanation.surface: A chaste romance that left a man named Horatio unsatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platonic affair' looks like a love affair without sex; here it is the business of Plato. Hamlet tells Horatio there are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in his — this answer — so it came up short.
explanation.definitionFit: The discipline Plato practised is the love of wisdom, and Hamlet tells Horatio his version cannot account for everything.

clue.text: Warning sound of an owl?

parts.note: a horn or siren that gives warning, and also a jocular name for a bird that hoots

explanation.definitionFit: A siren or horn gives a warning blast, and an owl is said to hoot.

clue.text: He'll be in touch about the play

definitions.text: He'll be in touch about the play

parts.words: He'll be in touch about the play
parts.note: an official who stands at the touchline in football or rugby and rules on the play

explanation.surface: A theatre agent promising to call back about a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touch' sounds like getting in contact and 'play' like a drama; in football and rugby, touch is the area beyond the side lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant referee patrols the side line and signals on the game.

clue.text: Position fielder where one can have a view

definitions.text: where one can have a view

parts.note: to take a stand is to take a position
point is a fielding position in cricket, and the fielder there

explanation.surface: A cricket captain placing a fielder where he can watch the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position square of the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint is a place, or a mental position, from which things are seen.

clue.text: Son looking ashen before fencing

indicators.note: before puts the word for looking ashen ahead of the abbreviation for son

parts.note: paling means turning pale, looking ashen

explanation.surface: A boy going white with fear before a fencing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests the sport; it is a fence of pointed stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed wooden stakes in a row make a fence.

clue.text: The old thing climbing in the Himalayas?

definitions.text: The old thing climbing in the Himalayas?

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word for thing is read upwards

parts.note: it can stand for a thing

explanation.surface: Some ancient creature scaling the peaks of the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' turns IT up into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a legendary ape-like creature said to roam the high Himalayas.

clue.text: Prudish girl that grows wild

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper, prudish
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A straitlaced young woman who runs wild.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow spring flower grows wild in British woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Resort petitions to keep down a poisonous bush

indicators.note: to keep down puts the letter from 'a' at the bottom of this down entry
to resort is to sort again, so the letters of petitions are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday town receives petitions to suppress a toxic shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town; read as re-sort, it rearranges PETITIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Christmas shrub with red leaves is often said to be toxic.

clue.text: Early form of English music originally had liveliness, so it's said

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of music
so it's said tells us the word for liveliness is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: brio means vigour or liveliness, especially in music

explanation.surface: A piece of English music that was spirited from the start, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn creature in its first stage of growth is its earliest form.

clue.text: Comeuppance, oddly, is the mot juste here

definitions.text: Comeuppance, oddly, is the mot juste here

parts.words: Comeuppance, oddly, is the mot juste here
parts.note: a deserved come-uppance, which is a fall from grace, is described by a word that oddly means the opposite of 'come up'

explanation.surface: A remark that a deserved punishment is strangely just the right word.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'come-uppance' contains COME UP, yet the word that fits it best is its opposite, a fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin or fall from power is the deserved punishment that a comeuppance brings.

clue.text: Paddy's Mini has run into trouble

indicators.note: running into trouble suggests the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An Irish person's small car has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Paddy is'; Paddy is a familiar nickname for a man from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddy is a common informal name for a man from Ireland, from the Irish name Pádraig.

clue.text: Stuff to swot up

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to pack something full
to swot up is to study hard just before an exam

explanation.definitionFit: Packing things tightly and studying intensively before a test are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: Growth of members of the Upper House, referred to as insane measure

definitions.text: Growth of members of the Upper House, referred to as

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy
a pint is a measure of beer

explanation.surface: Peers in the House of Lords dismissed as mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant is also called lords-and-ladies, so it is the growth named after members of the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild arum is commonly called lords-and-ladies, a plant named for peers.

clue.text: Passenger facing difficult situation in compartment

indicators.note: facing means standing in front of, so the bird comes before the predicament

parts.note: the passenger pigeon is an extinct North American bird, so a passenger is a kind of pigeon
to be in a hole is to be in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A traveller in a tricky spot inside a railway carriage compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passenger' points to a traveller; it is the passenger pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small open cubbyhole in a desk or wall rack, used for sorting letters, is a compartment.

clue.text: Defeated by what allowed extra runs, indefinite number.

parts.note: in cricket an overthrow is a fielder's throw that passes the stumps, letting the batsmen take more runs
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A cricket side beaten after giving away extra runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a wild return to the wicket that gives the batting side extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A government that has been toppled has been defeated.

clue.text: Barrister speaking for local authority

indicators.note: speaking tells us the word for barrister is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a barrister acting in court is counsel

explanation.surface: A lawyer acting as spokesperson for a town government.
explanation.definitionFit: A town or county is run by an elected body, the local authority.

clue.text: It's incumbent on the class to be performing well

parts.note: if a task is incumbent on you, it is up to you
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: Pupils are expected to do their best in lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's usual best means playing well.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts, perhaps, succeeded in dry barren area

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for succeeded inside the barren area

parts.note: a desert is a dry barren area
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: Someone finds fruit and nuts thriving in an arid wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit and nuts can be served as the sweet course at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Vital part of motoring that back-seat drivers will ignore

definitions.text: Vital part of motoring that back-seat drivers will ignore

parts.words: Vital part of motoring that back-seat drivers will ignore
parts.note: a car's exhaust muffler, and also something that keeps quiet, which nagging passengers disregard

explanation.surface: A gripe about passengers who ignore an essential rule of driving.
explanation.walkthrough: A back-seat driver is a passenger who keeps telling the driver what to do, so they ignore anything that would hush them.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhaust muffler quietens a car, and back-seat drivers never keep quiet.

clue.text: Securing ocean fish

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
ling is a long North Atlantic food fish related to cod

explanation.surface: Catching a fish from the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing something up tight, as with wax on an envelope, is fastening it.

clue.text: Unconscious and long-suffering, but not staying in hospital

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out
patient means enduring trouble without complaint

explanation.surface: A hospital case who is senseless and enduring but has been sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone treated at a hospital without being admitted overnight is a day patient.

clue.text: Currency runs into trouble in recession

indicators.note: into places the abbreviation for runs inside the other piece
in recession means going backwards, so the word for trouble is read from right to left

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A national currency runs into difficulty during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reads as economics; here it turns AIL round to LIA, and 'into' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Italy's monetary unit before the euro, and Turkey's still.

clue.text: Fiddle or tuba played regardless of tempo

indicators.note: to fiddle is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violin or tuba playing without keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin beside the tuba; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a tempo marking telling the player to speed up and slow down freely within a phrase.

clue.text: It's a drag, having slug in fungus

indicators.note: having means the first piece holds on to the second, which follows it

parts.note: a drag on a cigarette is a puff
a slug is a bullet, and ball is old military slang for bullets

explanation.surface: It is tedious finding a slimy slug inside a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' and 'slug' read as tedium and garden pest; they are a puff on a cigarette and a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: This round fungus releases a cloud of spores when burst.

clue.text: Unmarried girl said to be accomplished

indicators.note: said tells us the girl's name is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Mabel is a girl's name; un-married means removing M, the abbreviation for married, which leaves Abel

explanation.surface: A single woman reputed to be talented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried' is MABEL with M (married) removed, leaving ABEL, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled and competent is capable.

clue.text: One boy dressed as a monitor, for example

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ron is a boy's name
clad means dressed

explanation.surface: A schoolboy dressed up as a class monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A monitor is not a pupil here: USS Monitor was an armoured warship of the American Civil War, and gave its name to a class of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monitor was an armour-plated warship, and such steel-sheathed vessels are its class.

clue.text: Usual group of stars and luvvies at opening

parts.note: Norma is a southern constellation, the Carpenter's Square

indicators.note: at opening means only the first letter of luvvies is used

explanation.surface: Typical stage stars and luvvies turning up at a first night.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and standard both describe what is typical.

clue.text: Could "one more gin" be the basis of the Navy's power?

definitions.text: the basis of the Navy's power

indicators.note: could, asking what the quoted words might be, invites rearranging them

explanation.surface: A joke that a sailor's extra drink fuels the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship's motors are housed in the compartment that drives it.
